tia-infra: Heads up — eu-west-1 dedicated pool is hitting sustained GPU saturation. 15m avg ~98% and queuing is growing. Seeing autoscaler not placing new pods (AZ capacity errors).

alex-dev: confirmed from metrics — `gpu_util_pct{pool="dedicated-eu"} 98.3` and queue depth spiking, a few customer requests are getting routed to hosted fallback.

rachel-sre: @tia-infra @alex-dev any obvious config hits? autoscaler logs?

tia-infra: Autoscaler shows errors: `BatchPlacementError: InsufficientInstanceCapacity` from cloud provider for eu-west-1c. Tried `scale-up`, provider refusing due to regional spare GPU shortage.

sam-ml: Which customers are affected? Are fallbacks to hosted increasing cost significantly?

alex-dev: A small subset of Dedicated customers (reserved pools) are being routed to hosted. Latency up ~60-120ms for those requests and token cost delta ~2.5x per-token. I opened `#billing-watch` but we should minimize hosted spillover.

capacity-bot: autoscaler-alert: pool=dedicated-eu threshold=95% duration=00:12:00 action=fallback-to-hosted triggered=true

rachel-sre: Immediate mitigations: 1) throttle noncritical background batch jobs in dedicated-eu; 2) enable routing policy to prefer eu-west-2 dedicated if compatible; 3) pause canary rollouts that seed extra load. Will start 1 now.

tia-infra: Doing 1) and 3) now. Running command to reduce batch_workers for background queues: `infractl jobs scale --pool dedicated-eu --job background-train --replicas 0`

alex-dev: Running a quick routing change to divert new traffic to eu-west-2 dedicated if model variant and latency SLO allow: `routectl set-policy --pool dedicated-eu --failover-region eu-west-2 --threshold 90` — caution: cross-region adds latency for locality-sensitive customers.

ops-oncall: Noted. I'll notify support to message affected enterprise customers and offer temporary limits control. Also opening a provider capacity ticket (ref: #INC-7892).

sam-ml: For medium-term, can we spin up a smaller quantized instance class in eu-west-1 to soak inference (lower perf but saves hosted cost)? We have quantized variants ready.

tia-infra: Good idea. Spinning up a q4_0 pool as best-effort: `infractl gpu create --region eu-west-1 --type q4_0 --size 6 --label temp-quant` — if provider allows.

capacity-bot: provider-ticket:INC-7892 state=opened ETA=unknown

alex-dev: If provider denies, alternative is to increase prefix caching to reduce token work; lowering max_tokens for low-tier routes to reduce consumption. I'll patch routing config: `max_tokens: 512 -> 256` for tier=dev.

rachel-sre: Decision list: A) throttle background (done), B) prefer eu-west-2 dedicated where possible (in flight), C) try quantized pool in eu-west-1 (pending provider), D) notify customers (ops-oncall). Track cost delta from hosted spillover in the incident doc.

tia-infra: Pushing postmortem template into incident channel. I'll keep this thread updated. If eu-west-1 providers respond, I'll paste the ticket updates here. :rotating_light:

ops-oncall: Update 1750012530 — cloud provider replied: "Capacity constrained, offering spot-like GPUS with 24h eviction risk or provisioning in eu-west-2 only." They asked if we want spot.

sam-ml: Spot is risky for Dedicated customers. Decline for reserved pools. Use spot only for background/low-priority jobs.

alex-dev: Started re-routing low-priority traffic to hosted with cost tags so finance can track spike. `tagging: incident/1750012345`

rachel-sre: OK. If anyone sees any customer-visible errors, ping me. Otherwise we follow mitigation plan and await provider capacity or eu-west-2 scaling.

tia-infra: Last update for now 1750012700 — quantized pool creation request accepted for 6 GPUs in eu-west-1 (provisioning). Monitoring CPU/GPU + queue. Will report next.
